text.title: Latency Budget Allocation Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable latency signals to a rule from `content/01-core-rules.xml`. Every leaf names either a concrete rule id or `skip-this-methodology` when the case is out of scope. Max depth = 4.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a user-facing latency SLO stated as percentile + threshold + measurement point + window?

conclusion.verdict: skip-this-methodology: define the end-to-end SLO first; a budget cannot be allocated from a total that does not exist

branch.question: Does every hop on the critical path have a caller-side latency histogram with a named owner?

conclusion.verdict: instrument the unmeasured hops first; allocate only once each hop has a histogram and an owner

branch.question: Does any stage fan out to N parallel calls and wait for all of them?

conclusion.verdict: record N per stage and tighten the child percentile or add hedging before allocating the sequential hops

branch.question: Is any proposed hop budget below that hop's currently measured p95?

conclusion.verdict: link an improvement ticket with an owner for each underwater hop or raise its budget from the reserve before the gate goes live
run the procedure: verify the composition against the end-to-end histogram, fix bucket boundaries, fit timeouts and retries, emit the executable CI gate spec

text.example: Observable: SLO is p95 800 ms at the edge over 28 days; all five hops have caller-side histograms; the search stage fans out to 12 shards → r-fan-out-tightens-child-percentile: record N=12, budget each shard at a tighter percentile, then continue to the sequential allocation and the CI gate spec.
